decisions.reason: As a simple add-on to the core flooring business, the cleaning soap likely meets modest aspiration levels through cross-selling and service support, so boundedly rational management would keep it while uncertainty remains low.

The maintenance oil extends the established floor-care system and, in a growing market with some organisational slack, would likely be retained unless sales clearly fell short of aspiration for several periods.
This care product is somewhat more niche because it targets oiled floors, but it still fits the installed base and is more likely to be kept than dropped while management learns about demand.
A moisture-protection underlay complements floor sales and installation quality, so it likely stays unless performance is visibly below aspiration relative to comparable accessory products.
The high-density underlay foam is the most cull-prone accessory because it looks more substitutable and may overlap with other underlays, but current growth and slack still favor keeping it for now.

The oak parquet line is closest to the firm’s core capabilities and strategic direction, so management would usually keep it unless early market feedback showed a clear and persistent shortfall against aspiration.
